title: Best Bluetooth Speakers UK
short: Portable and smart Bluetooth speakers compared by sound quality, battery life and durability, from budget to premium.
intro: A good Bluetooth speaker balances sound quality, portability and durability, and the right choice depends on where you'll use it most. This guide compares speakers tested by Expert Reviews, which says it has tested more than 40 speakers since 2023, from budget picks to premium party speakers.

products.name: Flip 7
products.best_for: Most people who want a great everyday portable speaker
products.summary: Expert Reviews' overall favourite, balancing price, performance and portability better than anything else it has tested. Awesome power for its size with a super-durable design, though no USB-C cable is included.

products.name: Play
products.badge: Best for indoor and outdoor use
products.best_for: Buyers who want both Wi-Fi and Bluetooth flexibility
products.summary: Supports both Wi-Fi and Bluetooth with an included charging dock, delivering impactful, balanced sound, though the stereo presentation is unconvincing.

products.name: Beosound A1 3rd Gen
products.best_for: Buyers who want a design-led speaker that's also genuinely waterproof
products.summary: A gorgeous design paired with refined sound and IP67 waterproof and dropproof durability, at a premium price.

products.name: Grip
products.best_for: Buyers who want a fun, affordable speaker under £100
products.summary: A portable, budget-friendly speaker with punchy sound and built-in ambient lighting, though bass response is limited.

products.name: Zeppelin Pro
products.best_for: Buyers who prioritise sound quality above all else
products.summary: Sensational sound quality in a stylish design with multiple streaming options, though there's no remote control included.

products.name: MR1 Mk3
products.best_for: Buyers who want a speaker built for a desk rather than portability
products.summary: A desktop-friendly design with beautifully balanced sound and multiple connectivity options, though bass lacks depth.

products.name: Hyperboom
products.best_for: Large gatherings where volume matters most
products.summary: Loud and enjoyable sound with long-lasting battery, and the ability to pair with other UE Boom speakers, though it's large and heavy at 5.9kg.
pros: Can connect with other Boom speakers

products.name: Echo Dot Max
products.best_for: Buyers who want smart assistant features built in
products.summary: Effective Alexa integration with smart features and good sound quality for the price, though the light ring placement is a little awkward.

products.name: XBOOM XL7S
products.best_for: Buyers who want karaoke and DJ effects built in
products.summary: Fun karaoke and DJ effects with excellent lighting and powerful bass, splash-resistant to IPX4, though a microphone isn't included.

guide.q: What waterproof rating do I need?
guide.a: An IPX4 rating handles splashes, which suits a kitchen or a poolside table away from direct water. A full IP67 rating, like the Bang & Olufsen here, means the speaker can be briefly submerged, better suited to actually taking it in the pool or leaving it out in the rain.

Bluetooth speakers pair directly with a phone or laptop and work anywhere, with no home network needed. Wi-Fi speakers, or hybrid models like the Sonos Play here, can offer higher audio quality and multi-room features, but need a home network to unlock those extras.

guide.q: How much does size affect sound?
guide.a: Larger speakers generally produce deeper bass and higher maximum volume, which suits parties or outdoor gatherings. Smaller speakers trade some bass and volume for portability, better suited to a single room or travel.

guide.q: Is a smart speaker with Alexa or Google worth it?
guide.a: A built-in assistant like the Amazon Echo Dot Max here adds voice control, smart home integration and hands-free features, at the cost of some privacy considerations around an always-listening microphone. If you just want music playback, a standard Bluetooth speaker is simpler.
